phase: Mega Phase E, PR E1 -- continuous batching / scheduler foundation
design_summary: Replaced full-request-serialization (one std::mutex held for the whole generation) with bounded, genuinely concurrent decode. Deliberately NOT upstream llama.cpp's own shared-context/seq_id-slot design -- this project's per-request architecture (a brand-new llama_context per request, unchanged) is kept, because it is required by the existing real per-request adaptive planner (ctx sizing, KV quantization, GPU-layer split); a single shared context could not accommodate per-request-tuned parameters. Concurrency is bounded by decode_concurrency_gate_t (tools/membrane/decode_concurrency.h, default capacity 2, env MEMBRANE_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODE), which every request acquires (blocking, never rejecting) before its own membrane_session_generate() call. Each request operates on a real value COPY of the loaded model's session state, never the shared struct, avoiding a cross-request race on planner-output fields. A model switch drains (bounded ~5s wait) all in-flight decodes against the current model before closing it, reporting 503 MODEL_SWITCH_BUSY on timeout rather than corrupting anything.

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.title: membrane serve never suppressed llama.cpp's own verbose internal logging, causing a real hang class under bounded-buffer output sinks
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.root_cause: llama_log_set() was only ever called in membrane-run's own main.cpp (the CLI), never in server.cpp. Every chat request's fresh llama_context creation (unchanged 'persistent model, new context per request' architecture) printed ~13 KB of real llama.cpp-internal diagnostic output (graph_reserve/sched_reserve/resolve_fused_ops) to stderr, measured directly on the real SmolLM2-135M fixture, four requests producing 51554 bytes.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.impact: Under any real supervisor/harness whose stdout/stderr sink has bounded buffering and no continuous reader (confirmed and reproduced directly: Python subprocess.PIPE without a draining thread -- NOT systemd/journald, which reads continuously), enough real sequential requests (~5 measured) fill the OS pipe buffer and the request-handling thread's own fprintf() call blocks forever, starving every other request waiting on that thread's held decode-gate/admission slot.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.diagnosis_method: /proc/<pid>/task/*/wchan inspection on the live, stuck process confirmed the stuck thread was genuinely blocked in anon_pipe_write, not in any lock/condvar this project's own code owns -- ruled out a scheduler deadlock directly rather than assumed.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.fix: tools/membrane/server.cpp: membrane_server_run() now calls llama_log_set(membrane_server_log_callback, NULL) once at startup (ERROR-level only passed through), mirroring main.cpp's own quiet_log_callback.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.verified: Re-ran the exact same real 6-request sequence after the fix: stdout stayed at 52 bytes (just the startup banner). Re-ran the full verify-continuous-batching.py suite: all checks now PASS (previously 3/5 failed with 60s client-side timeouts).

real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.id: E1-FINDING-1 (not a bug fixed in this PR -- disclosed, third-party, pre-existing)
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.title: A real TSan-flagged data race exists inside vendored ggml's own CPU-backend intra-op compute kernels (ggml_compute_forward_flash_attn_ext_f16_one_chunk / ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat_one_chunk)
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.attribution: Confirmed NOT caused by E1's own cross-request scheduler: reproduces identically with MEMBRANE_MAX_CONCURRENT_DECODE=1 and exactly ONE in-flight request (zero cross-request concurrency) -- ggml's own n_threads=4 intra-op worker threads (spawned via libgomp for that single context's own decode) race on writes into that same context's own compute buffer. This has been real and present since n_threads>1 was first used (long before this phase); it was simply never exercised under a TSan build with real generation before (the existing CI TSan job, test_server.cpp, deliberately stays real-generation-free via a nonexistent-model 404 path).
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.scope_decision: NOT fixed in this PR -- patching vendored, third-party ggml CPU-kernel source is well outside a scheduler-foundation PR's scope, and real output was observed correct/coherent in every request despite the warnings (consistent with a class of hand-tuned numeric-kernel races that are benign in practice on real hardware but technically flagged by TSan's memory model). Does not affect CI (the CI TSan job's own real-generation-free design is unaffected and stays green). Disclosed honestly in docs/soak-and-concurrency-testing.md rather than hidden or wrongly attributed to E1's own new code.
real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_this_ph.e1_own_code_status: decode_concurrency_gate_t, decode_slot_enter/decode_slot_exit, the per-request local_session copy, and ensure_model_loaded's drain-wait show NO TSan-flagged races in isolation, including under real concurrent generation.
